_meta.purpose: Tier-B research allow-list. These pages are READ LIVE by the advisor when a question warrants it (opt-in per question), with citations. They are NOT scraped into adapters and never touch the valuation — ros_points / marginal stay computed from each league's own scraped ESPN scoring (docs/contracts.md guardrail 6).
_meta.tier_a_is_elsewhere: The structured adapters live in scraping/sources/ (fantasypros, borischen, sleeper, fantasycalc, nflverse). Anything in THIS file is deliberately not an adapter: HTML-only, no public API, or too low-volume to be worth a nightly parse.
_meta.usage: An advisor may fetch any url whose entry is in `allow`. Entries in `dead` are recorded so nobody re-adds them.

allow.name: FantasyPros — rest-of-season consensus (all scoring variants)
allow.what_its_good_for: Human-readable view of the same ECR the fantasypros adapter ingests. Useful for reading expert NOTES and the per-player spread, which the JSON blob only summarises. Swap the slug for ros-ppr-overall.php / ros-half-point-ppr-overall.php to match a league's scoring.

allow.name: FantasyPros — weekly positional rankings
allow.what_its_good_for: This week's consensus with expert commentary. Slug pattern: {''|ppr-|half-point-ppr-}{qb|rb|wr|te|k|dst|flex}.php — QB/K/DST have no scoring variant.

allow.name: FantasyPros — injury news
allow.what_its_good_for: Beat-reporter injury notes with timestamps. The reason a snap share collapsed, which nflverse can only show you the effect of.

allow.name: FantasyPros — team depth charts
allow.what_its_good_for: Current depth and role. Replaces the Footballguys depth-chart page, which is dead. Use when deciding whether a backup is one snap from value.

allow.name: FantasyPros — trade tools
allow.what_its_good_for: A second market opinion on a specific trade, to sanity-check the fantasycalc value the trade finder uses.

allow.name: FantasyPros — stat leaders / usage reports
allow.what_its_good_for: Red-zone looks, snap counts and target leaders in one place when the nflverse assets are stale or a week behind.

allow.name: Razzball Football
allow.what_its_good_for: Waiver-wire columns and streaming picks with reasoning. Strong on the 'who is the add this week' question that a raw ranking does not answer.

allow.name: Razzball — rest-of-season rankings
allow.what_its_good_for: An independent ROS opinion to set against FantasyPros consensus. NOTE: the canonical URL redirects to a year-stamped post, so check the date on what you land on before quoting it.
allow.verified: 2026-09-14 · 200 (redirects to a dated post — verify the season)

allow.name: FFToday — rest-of-way rankings
allow.what_its_good_for: Rest-of-way projections by position. Pattern: playerrank.php?o=2&PosID={10 QB,20 RB,30 WR,40 TE,80 K,99 DST}; o=1 is the preseason set, o=2 is rest-of-way. Weekly is playerwkrank.php.
allow.verified: 2026-09-14 · 200 (the old playerRoSproj.php slug is 404 — use playerrank.php?o=2)

allow.name: TeamRankings — NFL stat pages
allow.what_its_good_for: Points-allowed-by-position and pace/efficiency splits — the replacement for the dead games.espn.go.com 'points against' page. Game-environment context for a streaming decision.

allow.name: TeamRankings — NFL odds and lines (Vegas)
allow.what_its_good_for: Spreads and totals. Implied team total is the single best one-number proxy for game environment; a 27-point implied total changes a streaming call more than two ranking slots do.

allow.name: TeamRankings — opponent points per game
allow.what_its_good_for: Direct defensive strength lookup when evaluating a D/ST stream or a matchup-based start/sit.

allow.name: NFL Weather
allow.what_its_good_for: Wind and precipitation by game. Wind above ~15mph is the only weather variable that reliably moves kicker and passing output. JS-rendered with no tables, which is exactly why it is Tier B and not an adapter. Week pages: /week/{season}/week-{N}.

allow.name: Rotowire — NFL
allow.what_its_good_for: Fast player-news feed with fantasy impact lines. Good for 'what happened in the last 12 hours' before a waiver run.

allow.name: Rotowire — NFL news feed
allow.what_its_good_for: The raw chronological feed, when you want everything since the last check rather than the curated front page.

allow.name: NBC Sports Fantasy (formerly Rotoworld)
allow.what_its_good_for: Analysis columns and player notes. This is where rotoworld.com now lives — link to this, never to the old domain.

allow.name: FF Librarian
allow.what_its_good_for: Directory of fantasy tools and articles — the useful residue of the r/fantasyfootball resources wiki, kept current by a human. Use it to find a tool, not as a data source. HTTP ONLY: its https endpoint fails the TLS handshake, so fetch over http.

dead.name: Footballguys depth charts
dead.note: superseded by the FantasyPros team pages in `allow`

dead.name: KFFL
dead.status: redirects to thehuddle.com; its tools are gone

dead.name: Rotoworld
dead.note: use the NBC Sports Fantasy entry in `allow`

dead.name: Pro Football Reference
dead.note: excellent data, but it blocks automated fetches; nflverse carries the same underlying numbers

dead.name: Twitter/X beat-writer list
dead.status: no free API; the wiki's ~400 handles are flagged out-of-date at source
dead.note: not ingestible. The useful residue is the NAMES — put them in the league briefing as 'whose reporting to weight', not as a feed.
